findings.title: Booking cancellation does not await workflow reminder cancellations
findings.body: handleCancelBooking cancels workflow reminders by calling async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder inside nested forEach loops and never awaits the returned promises or includes them in the request's awaited promises. The handler can return before SendGrid/Twilio cancellations and Prisma updates/deletes finish; in serverless deployments the unfinished work may be terminated. As a result, reminders for cancelled bookings can still be sent, which is the exact issue this PR is trying to fix.

findings.title: Reschedule endpoint does not await old reminder cancellations
findings.body: In requestReschedule, bookingToReschedule.workflowReminders.forEach calls async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder without awaiting them. The tRPC mutation can complete before the old booking's reminders are actually marked cancelled/deleted or canceled with the provider, so old reminders may still be delivered.

findings.title: Rescheduled booking reminder cancellation is fire-and-forget and bypasses deferred cancel
findings.body: handleNewBooking cancels the original booking's reminders in a forEach without awaiting the async calls, so the surrounding try/catch cannot catch failures and the request may finish before cancellation completes. It also passes immediateDelete=true for email reminders; if the immediate SendGrid cancellation fails, no cancelled flag or DB cleanup is left for retry. Old reminders from a rescheduled booking can therefore still be sent.

findings.title: Workflow deletion cancels scheduled emails fire-and-forget before cascade delete
findings.body: In the workflow delete mutation, scheduledReminders.forEach calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true)/deleteScheduledSMSReminder without awaiting. The workflow is then deleted, cascading away WorkflowReminder rows. If the external SendGrid/Twilio cancellation does not complete or fails, there is no DB state left to retry, and scheduled emails/SMS for the deleted workflow may still be sent.

findings.title: Workflow update cancels reminders without awaiting provider/DB operations
findings.body: When removing event types from a workflow, and similarly when deleting/editing steps around lines 519 and 574, the update mutation calls async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder inside forEach without awaiting. The mutation can return before reminders are marked cancelled or canceled, and errors are swallowed. Stale reminders may remain active and be sent.

findings.title: Cron authentication can pass when CRON_API_KEY is unset
findings.body: The cron handler compares process.env.CRON_API_KEY with the supplied apiKey using strict inequality. If CRON_API_KEY is not configured, both sides are undefined for a request with no key, so the endpoint is accessible without authentication. This endpoint can cancel and schedule workflow emails, so it should require a configured CRON_API_KEY and reject unauthenticated requests.

findings.title: Cron cancellation query is too broad and can include rows without a SendGrid batch id
findings.body: scheduleEmailReminders selects remindersToCancel only by cancelled=true and scheduledDate. It does not filter method=EMAIL, scheduled=true, or referenceId not null. The loop then sends reminder.referenceId as batch_id to SendGrid. A row with a null/invalid referenceId, or a non-email reminder if cancelled is ever set, can make the request fail; due to the surrounding error handling, that can prevent other valid cancellations from being processed.

findings.title: A single failure aborts the whole cron cancellation loop
findings.body: The cancellation logic awaits each SendGrid request inside one try/catch around the whole for loop. If any request throws, such as from rate limiting, a network error, or an invalid batch id, control jumps to catch and the remaining reminders are neither canceled in SendGrid nor deleted from WorkflowReminder. Those reminders can still be sent. Each reminder should be canceled with independent error handling.

findings.title: Cron may schedule stale reminders without checking booking status or cancelled flag
findings.body: The unscheduledReminders query filters only method=EMAIL, scheduled=false, and scheduledDate. It does not exclude cancelled=true rows and does not require the related booking to still be ACCEPTED. If a reminder row remains after a booking is cancelled/rescheduled, which is possible because cancellation calls are fire-and-forget or can race, the cron will schedule and send an email for that booking.

findings.title: immediateDelete cancels SendGrid but leaves no reliable DB state
findings.body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder's immediateDelete branch posts a cancellation to SendGrid and returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder row or marking cancelled=true. In reschedule flows this leaves stale scheduled reminder rows. More importantly, if the SendGrid call fails, the function catches/logs and returns success, so there is no retryable state and the originally scheduled email may still be sent.

findings.title: Paid booking cancellation returns before cancelling workflow reminders
findings.body: In handleCancelBooking, the paid branch refunds the booking, updates it to REJECTED, and returns before the later code that cancels workflow reminders. Therefore cancelled paid bookings can retain scheduled workflow reminders. Since the PR is intended to stop reminders for cancelled bookings, this early return should also perform the reminder cancellation or move cancellation before the return.
